title: Choose the visual world — round 2
question: The roll assigned The Schedule of Risks. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll again.

options.label: The Schedule of Risks
options.lineage: the insurance policy schedule and the adjuster's claim form
options.thesis: The corpus is a schedule of one hundred risks, each with a quantity, a rate, an amount and a note that qualifies it. The dossier reads as the adjuster's own claim form: every number is a line item with a basis, and the margin holds the pencil note that keeps the estimate honest.
options.viewport: The schedule header: Insured, Policy, Period, Territory (the two corridors), Limit (Rs 2,24 lakh a month of addressable demand), Deductible (Rs 850 a clustered visit), Premium floor (Rs 1,100). Under it the first claim form: the ten strongest localities as line items, each with a basis, a quantity, a rate and an amount, and the adjuster's note in the right margin. The verdict is an underwriting stamp, slightly off-register, above the key figure. The way forward is the schedule index: fifteen route clusters, each with its acceptance mark.
options.risk: A policy schedule reads as a contract, and a contract is a promise. Half this corpus rests on a modelled household base, and a stamped schedule makes tier C look as settled as tier A. Three rules are not negotiable: no figure shown without its tier, the note column never becomes a footnote, and the stamp never claims a figure is measured.

raised.raise: THE HOUSE SET. The ten divisions take ten sheet tints from one fixed house palette, hard-cut between them, never a fade, so a reader knows where they are before they read the rail.
THE FOLD-OUT APPENDIX. The hundred-row register deploys from a folded summary into the full sheet, and the full table is always present for print and for assistive technology.
THE ONE DIAGRAM THAT TEACHES. The twenty-four hour curve arrives as a single annotated diagram a reader can follow without the prose, drawn with the adjuster's pencil and nothing else.

options.label: The Chennai Street Directory
options.lineage: the bound city directory of classified entries
options.thesis: A hundred localities are a hundred entries: name, ward, category, address, telephone, hours. The dossier becomes the directory a pet parent would look up, with the analyst's ratings and notes in the margin.
options.viewport: The directory's front matter: the edition, the territory it covers, and the index of one hundred entries by ward. Each entry is a ruled block with its name, ward, category, count and note.
options.risk: A searchable list of places is the obvious shape for a hundred localities, and most runs in this category land here. It is effective and it is the safe answer.

options.label: Centre-Rail Reference Setting
options.lineage: a reference-setting page drawn by a ruling engine
options.thesis: Two short columns twinned around a fixed centre rail of keys, the whole block held small inside a wide annotation margin where the apparatus hangs and overlaps the block's edge.
options.viewport: A ruled block: two columns of small roman round a vermilion centre rail carrying keys and square detents cut wherever the flow changes footing. The annotation margin holds the apparatus, overlapping the block's edge.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: the centre rail is a real table of contents for a hundred risks and the annotation margin is exactly where caveats belong. Loses narrowly: a setting apparatus says the reader is reading a work of reference, and this is a decision.
options.risk: The vermilion rail competes with the notes it is meant to carry, and a two-column block at 34 characters a column is slow on a phone.

options.label: Daylight Section
options.lineage: a daylight section, the sun cutting luminous rooms through a building
options.thesis: The working day drawn in section. The sunbeam's gold is the active band, shadow blue is the withdrawn hour, and the reading is a long continuous section with architect's inclined lettering and tabular time stamps.
options.viewport: One long section ruled across the sheet, the hours as a horizontal datum, the peak window picked out in gold and the closed hours in shadow blue, annotations pinned to the light angles.
options.case: Fuses cleanly on the hour story, and time as the organising axis is the right spine for a dossier about when demand happens. Loses on identification: a daylight section says architecture, and this is a market.
options.risk: A drawing with one golden band can imply a precision the hour data does not have.

options.label: Normalled Jackfield
options.lineage: a jackfield normalling schedule on unlit black glass
options.thesis: Every item tied to its default by an amber link line that is unbroken, cross-ticked, gapped, doubled or ended in an open ring. State is drawn by stroke pattern, never by hue.
options.viewport: An endless lane grid drifting under a fixed left legend strip, each row's link rail carrying its own state by stroke pattern. Dark gutters at both edges mean nothing spans full width.
options.case: Best of the six at carrying state without colour, and the broken-line discipline is exactly right for a corpus that must never imply a live figure is a settled one. Loses on identification: it is an instrument, and the reader is underwriting a business.
options.risk: Black glass behind a hundred rows is heavy on a phone, and a link rail reads as configuration rather than evidence.

options.label: Plakatstil Object Poster Wall
options.lineage: a Berlin poster house's trade-mark wall
options.case: Fuses poorly: a wall of saturated grounds and heroic flat objects reads as a showcase of goods, and this corpus is a hundred risks with notes attached.
options.kept: Kept as RAISE 1, THE HOUSE SET, a fixed palette of sheet tints as a per-unit custom property, hard-cut and never faded.

options.label: Miura-Fold Deployable Sheet
options.lineage: a vast pleated sheet unfolding from a hand-sized packet
options.case: Fuses poorly: a fold is an instrument, and on a reading surface it becomes a mechanism in front of the argument.
options.kept: Kept as RAISE 2, THE FOLD-OUT APPENDIX, the hundred-row register deployed from a folded summary with the full table always present for print and for assistive technology.

options.label: Hand-Drawn Technical Zine
options.case: Fuses poorly: mascots and marker lettering would launder a research corpus into an explainer, and this brand states that the market floor is loss-making.
options.kept: Kept as RAISE 3, THE ONE DIAGRAM THAT TEACHES, the hour curve as a single annotated diagram readable without the prose.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What this category ships, executed impeccably: a clean grid, a headline, a chart, a table.
canonCard.viewport: The arrangement a visitor expects, at full craft.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
